meta.location: Ammonihah and the land of Noah
principles: A prediction made and acted on

world_behind.title: Mormon dates the attack to the day
world_behind.text: Verse 1 gives the eleventh month, the tenth day, of the nineteenth year. He rarely dates anything this precisely.

world_behind.title: Ammonihah had been destroyed once
world_behind.text: Verse 3 says the Lamanites levelled it in Alma 16 and expected an easy prey. The city's reputation is the trap.

world_behind.title: Mormon corrects himself mid-verse
world_behind.text: Verse 3 has him say the city had been rebuilt, then stop and say it was rebuilt in part. The correction stays on the page.

world_behind.title: The Lamanites had upgraded their own equipment
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says they came with shields, breastplates, and thick garments of skins. Alma 43 had them nearly naked, so they learned from the last war.

world_behind.title: Amalickiah stayed home
world_behind.text: Verses 10 and 11 say that if he had come he might have driven the attack through, because he did not care for the blood of his people. He sent captains instead.

world_behind.title: Moroni predicted the second target
world_behind.text: Verse 15 says he supposed they would be frightened at Ammonihah and march for Noah, the weakest place, so he made Noah the strongest.

world_behind.title: The casualty figures are exact and lopsided
world_behind.text: Verse 23 gives more than a thousand Lamanites dead and not one Nephite. Verse 24 adds about fifty wounded, and says where the wounds were.

words.text: A raised bank of earth. The word occurs once in scripture. Mormon uses it for the work at Ammonihah that put the defenders out of range and left only one way in.

Fortified works. The phrase forts of security occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible, both in this chapter. Verse 13 says Moroni had built them for every city in all the land round about.
The one gap in the works. The word occurs seven times in this record and eleven in the King James Bible. Four of the seven are in this chapter, and the whole battle is fought at the thing it names.

A trench dug for defense. The record uses the word four times and the King James Bible six, none of them military. Alma 53 has Lamanite prisoners digging one at Bountiful. Here it pairs with the bank as the two halves of the design.
Vast. The phrase immense slaughter occurs once in scripture. Mormon uses it of what happened at the entrance, and verse 23 supplies the number behind the word.
A way through. Mormon uses the noun twice in this verse for the gap the Lamanites tried to make, which the record distinguishes from the entrance they could not force.

phrases.term: They supposed that it would again become an easy prey for them
phrases.text: The Lamanite reasoning, and it is sound from what they knew. Ammonihah had fallen before, so they went back to it. Moroni had counted on the reasoning.
Mormon writes the battle from the attacker's point of view. Disappointed and astonished appear five times across the chapter, and they carry the narrative more than the fighting does.

phrases.term: They had also prepared themselves with garments of skins, yea, very thick garments
phrases.text: The Lamanites solved the last war's problem. Alma 43 had them naked against armored men; here they arrive dressed for it, and it makes no difference against earthworks.

phrases.term: They were prepared for them, in a manner which never had been known among the children of Lehi
phrases.text: Mormon claims the fortifications were unprecedented in six hundred years of the record. He credits them to the instructions of Moroni in the same verse.

phrases.term: He did care not for the blood of his people
phrases.text: Mormon's judgment on the absent king. It is offered as the reason the attack might have succeeded had he come, which makes indifference to casualties a military advantage.

phrases.term: Moroni had altered the management of affairs among the Nephites
phrases.text: The change is described as administrative. What defeated the invasion was a decision about how places are held, taken before anyone marched.

phrases.term: This was wisdom in Moroni; for he had supposed that they would be frightened at the city Ammonihah
phrases.text: Mormon states the prediction and its reasoning. Moroni expected the enemy to move to the weakest point, so he made the weakest point the strongest, and verse 14 says it worked.

phrases.term: Their chief captains had sworn with an oath to attack the city
phrases.text: The Lamanites are afraid of Lehi and attack anyway because of a promise made in verse 13. An oath taken before the reconnaissance drives the assault.

phrases.term: Instead of filling up their ditches by pulling down the banks of earth, they were filled up in a measure with their dead
phrases.text: Mormon turns the engineering into the image. The trench the Lamanites meant to level gets filled by the men sent to level it.

phrases.term: There was not a single soul of the Nephites which was slain
phrases.text: The count, given against more than a thousand on the other side. Mormon states it flatly and then qualifies it in the next verse.

phrases.term: Their wounds were upon their legs, many of which were very severe
phrases.text: Fifty wounded, and Mormon says where. The armor covered everything except what the arrows could reach through the pass, which is a detail only someone thinking about the equipment would record.

verses.label: v. 1–5
verses.title: At Ammonihah
verses.text: The Lamanite armies appear in the eleventh month. The city is partly rebuilt and an army is stationed at its borders behind cast-up dirt. A ridge of earth puts the defenders out of range and leaves one entrance. The Lamanite captains are astonished at the preparation.

verses.label: v. 6–9
verses.title: What they expected
verses.text: They came with numbers, shields, breastplates, and thick skin garments, expecting to overpower the Nephites and take them into bondage or kill them at pleasure. Instead they met a preparation never known among the children of Lehi, made after Moroni's instructions.

verses.label: v. 10–13
verses.title: The absent king
verses.text: Had Amalickiah come, he might have pressed the attack, since he did not care for his people's blood. He stayed, and his captains would not attack. They marched for the land of Noah, not knowing Moroni had fortified every city, and their captains swore to destroy it.

verses.label: v. 14–17
verses.title: Noah made strong
verses.text: Noah had been the weakest place and was now stronger than Ammonihah. Moroni had expected them to be frightened off the first city and to come to the second, and it fell out as he desired. Lehi commanded there, and the Lamanites feared him, but the oath held them to the attack.

verses.label: v. 18–20
verses.title: The works
verses.text: The bank was too high and the ditch too deep to enter anywhere but the pass. Nephites stood ready to throw stones and arrows at anyone climbing, and their strongest men waited at the entrance with swords and slings.

verses.label: v. 21–22
verses.title: The assault
verses.text: The Lamanite captains brought their armies to the entrance and were driven back repeatedly with immense slaughter. They tried to dig down the banks to make their own pass and were swept off, and the ditch filled with their own dead and wounded.

verses.label: v. 23–25
verses.title: The count
verses.text: The Lamanites kept attacking until every one of their chief captains was killed, more than a thousand dead, and not one Nephite slain. About fifty were wounded through the pass, their armor holding except on the legs. The survivors fled to report the loss to Amalickiah.

chapter.title: The battle is won before it starts
chapter.text: Verse 15 gives the prediction and verse 14 gives the result. The fighting in verses 21 and 22 only confirms a decision taken months earlier.

chapter.title: Mormon writes it from the losing side
chapter.text: Disappointment, astonishment, and expectation drive the account. The reader is shown what the Lamanites thought would happen and then what met them.

chapter.title: Both sides learned from the last war and only one learning mattered
chapter.text: The Lamanites fixed their armor problem; Moroni changed where the fighting would happen. The second answer beat the first.

chapter.title: An oath forces a bad attack
chapter.text: The captains feared Lehi and had already sworn. Alma 44 had Zerahemnah refuse an oath he knew he would break; here men keep one they should not have made.

chapter.title: The absent commander is the reason it failed
chapter.text: Mormon says plainly that Amalickiah's willingness to spend lives might have carried the works. The chapter credits the Nephite victory partly to his staying home.

chapter.title: The ditch becomes the argument
chapter.text: Men sent to fill a trench fill it with themselves. Mormon lets the engineering carry the moral without adding one.

chapter.title: The count is stated and then honestly qualified
chapter.text: Not one slain, then about fifty wounded, then where the wounds were. Mormon gives the striking number and immediately makes it precise.

chapter.title: The equipment detail is the tell
chapter.text: Wounds on the legs, because shields, breastplates, and head-plates covered the rest. The record is tracking what the armor did, verse by verse, across three chapters.

applications.title: Strengthen where they will actually come
applications.text: Moroni worked out where the attack would move to and fortified that. When you are preparing for trouble, think one step past the obvious point of failure.

applications.title: Let a bad reputation work for you
applications.text: Ammonihah looked like an easy target and was not. What people assume about your weak spot is information you can use.

applications.title: Do not swear before you have looked
applications.text: The captains bound themselves to an attack and then found Lehi commanding. Delay the commitment until after the reconnaissance.

applications.title: Correct yourself in the sentence
applications.text: Mormon said rebuilt, then said in part rebuilt. When you notice you have overstated something, fix it immediately rather than letting it stand.

questions.text: What do people assume about me that is out of date?
What problem have I solved thoroughly that has stopped being the problem?
Whose indifference to cost makes them dangerous?
What have I changed in how things are managed rather than in how hard I work?
Where is my weakest point, and have I told anyone?
What have I sworn to that I would not choose now?
Where am I unprotected, and is it somewhere I can cover?
